name: Sickly Green
lede: Sickly Green is a strong, murky yellow-green recorded in the 2010 xkcd color survey, where respondents reached for the look of nausea rather than a plant, place or pigment to name it.

sections.title: A feeling, not a thing
sections.body:
The 2010 xkcd survey gathered 1,058,212 free-text color names from 127,825 participants shown random hex values, and Munroe published roughly the top thousand that emerged [1]. "Sickly" describes an association, the color of nausea or illness, rather than naming a dye, mineral or place [1]. By our look-alike data its nearest colors are [[avocado|Avocado]], 2.5 units away, and [[avocado-green|Avocado Green]], 3.3 units away, both read as almost the same [2].

No dictionary, standard or paint company lists this name; the 2010 survey is its only documented appearance [1]. [[pea-soup-green|Pea Soup Green]] sits a little further off, 3.8 units away, another food name crowded into the same yellow-green corner [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to this yellow-green in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [3]. All three are Scandinavian or French landscape works from 1888 to 1941, the earliest Odilon Redon's 1888 *Peyrelebade*, a floor set by the archive's own holdings rather than a true first sighting [3]. Denmark shows the largest lift of any country checked, 2 hits across 1,676 Danish paintings, though on a sample too thin for a real claim about Danish painting generally [3]. The color's rarity in art fits a name born from an emotional reaction rather than from pigment use [3].
